lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Early, private shorthand: Elizabeth says she understood his words better than he thought.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: A vivid domestic moment: Flush’s ecstatic reunion with Elizabeth.

lines.text: Friday will come however,—and I may as well go on to tell you that Mrs. Jameson came yesterday.
lines.note: Mrs Jameson arrives asking ‘Anything settled?’, showing how close their secret is to exposure.
A tiny, odd exclamation that feels like a private joke between them.

lines.text: Here is the bad news going to you as fast as bad news will go! for you ‘do really (NOT) see me to-morrow,’ Robert,—there is no chance of it for such ‘too, two’ wise people as we are!
lines.note: Elizabeth reverses the expected meeting with abrupt bad news.

lines.text: I was beginning to dress, hours before the proper time, through the confidence of seeing you now,—after the letter which came early in the morning,—when this new letter changes everything.
lines.note: Robert caught dressing hours early, then undone by her changed letter.

lines.text: Here is a distress for me, dearest!
lines.note: Flush is stolen, a major turn in the story.

lines.text: I am sure you are grieved and frightened for our friend and follower, that was to be, at Pisa—will you not write a special note to tell me when you get him again?
lines.note: Robert calls Flush ‘our friend and follower, that was to be.’

lines.text: ‘Our friend and follower, that was to be’—is that, then, your opinion of my poor darling Flush’s destiny— Ah,—I should not have been so quiet if I had not known differently and better.
lines.note: Elizabeth quotes Robert’s ‘friend and follower’ phrase back to him.

lines.text: Was ever any in the world, in any possible world, so perfectly good and dear to another as you are to me!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s sweeping, specific praise of Robert’s goodness.

lines.text: You will only expect a few words—what will those be?
lines.note: Robert’s full-heart note after the wedding day.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s exhausted, immediate wedding-day note that all is safe.

lines.text: Thank you a thousand times for the note, my own Ba.
lines.note: Robert’s gratitude for her proof of love.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Final anticipation that by the next day they will have only each other.
